# Regex fixtures for skill: panel
# Format: one directive per non-empty, non-comment line.
#   MATCH: <prompt>     — regex from config/default-triggers.json for this skill must match
#   NO_MATCH: <prompt>  — regex must NOT match
# Tested deterministically by tests/test-regex-fixtures.sh (zero LLM cost).
# First NO_MATCH line is verbatim-borrowed from the design-debate MATCH fixture.
# Remaining NO_MATCH lines pin the explicit-model-intent boundary (design decision 5):
# routine engineering language must not route here.
#
# Panel is the SEVERAL-models method. Its single-model clause moved to `second-opinion`,
# which carries the same outbound-data controls -- that ORDER matters: moving the clause
# first, before those controls existed, was a security regression. Panel gained a
# two-named-participants clause so an explicit multi-model ask is still claimed here.

MATCH: run a panel of models on this design
MATCH: ask codex, gemini and gpt-5 each for their take on this design
MATCH: i want a cross-model review of the caching tradeoff
MATCH: give me a model panel on these two options
# NOT a trigger case any more: "run a standalone panel on this question" names no model,
# and every panel trigger now requires an AI-participant token (model/llm/named vendor)
# because delivery words alone matched legal, finance, science and HR prose. It still
# routes, via the NAME boost -- "run a ... panel" is deliberate naming. Asserted in
# tests/test-routing.sh, not here; this file tests triggers only.
NO_MATCH: run a standalone panel on this question; return independent raw answers
MATCH: get independent answers from several models and show them to me unmerged

NO_MATCH: let's debate the tradeoffs between a monolith and microservices architecture
NO_MATCH: cross-check the config against the fallback registry
NO_MATCH: add an independent perspectives section to the report
NO_MATCH: get a second opinion from the reviewer before merging
NO_MATCH: add a task codex entry to the backlog
NO_MATCH: get a second opinion from another model on this migration plan
NO_MATCH: ask codex to weigh in on this approach
NO_MATCH: consult codex about the schema change
NO_MATCH: the collapsible panel on the settings screen needs a scrollbar
NO_MATCH: add an independent panel widget to the dashboard

# INFRASTRUCTURE-PROSE DECOYS (added after adversarial review found 11 false dispatches,
# 8 of them to skills that ship repo content to an external vendor). The first cut of
# these contract triggers was measured against an INVENTED negative corpus that had no
# MLOps/agent-infrastructure prose in it at all -- the one domain where "model", "agent",
# "response", "counter" and "exchange" are ordinary nouns. Every line below MATCHED a
# shipped trigger and routed outbound. Do not relax the clauses that keep them silent.

# PER-CLAUSE COVERAGE IS LOAD-BEARING (mutation-verified 2026-09-16).
# Every trigger clause for this skill is depended on by at least one MATCH line above:
# blanking any single clause in config/default-triggers.json produces >=1 failing
# assertion here. Verified by emptying each clause in turn in a scratch copy --
# design-debate 1-4, panel 2-3, synthesize 0 -- all 7 caught.
#
# CORRECTION to the commit message of 342221f, which claimed "fixtures alone would NOT
# have caught" a silently-empty extracted regex. That is FALSE as written. It was true
# only in the window before these MATCH lines existed. Keep it true: when you ADD a
# trigger clause, add a MATCH line that fails without it -- otherwise a neutered clause
# ships green.

# CROSS-DOMAIN DECOYS (second adversarial pass, Codex). The first narrowing still routed
# these outbound: delivery words like "verbatim" and "side by side" are ordinary
# formatting vocabulary in legal, finance, scientific, HR and education writing, and
# "agents" is robotics/simulation vocabulary. Every panel and design-debate trigger now
# requires an AI-participant token (model/llm/named vendor); these lines fail if that
# requirement is ever relaxed back to delivery words or bare reciprocals.

# TWO NAMED VENDORS => panel, WHATEVER THE VERB (round-5 finding, and a regression I
# introduced). second-opinion gained "put|paste|send|take|give|hand" for its own recall
# fix; panel's two-vendor clause still listed only ask|consult|poll|get|run, so
# "put this to codex and gemini separately" routed to the ONE-model skill. That is a
# contract violation, not a miss: the user asked for several models and would have got
# one. The verb sets are now aligned. Naming two participants is the signal; the verb is not.
MATCH: put this to codex and gemini separately and show me what each one says
MATCH: paste this question to codex and gemini and show both answers
MATCH: ask codex and claude for their take on this schema

# TWO VENDORS + a panel cue, without needing a leading verb (round-5 structural misses).
# The shared primitive is "two named vendors in one breath" -- already the strongest
# signal this repo has -- combined with a per-skill cue, rather than ten bespoke patterns
# for ten phrasings. Gated against the full 206-prompt accumulated negative corpus: zero
# new false positives.
MATCH: same prompt to gpt-5 and to claude, clean contexts, raw answers labelled by who said what

# CSS LAYOUT PROSE (round-6 false dispatch, and the only one it found). The vendor-free
# clause required TWO signals -- a plural source and a raw-delivery word -- and
# "the two columns stop sitting side by side" satisfies BOTH in pure layout vocabulary.
# Two signals are not enough when both are ordinary UI words. The clause now also requires
# an ANSWER-noun near the delivery word, because the contract is about ANSWERS delivered
# raw, not about layout. Fixed at no recall cost.

NO_MATCH: the two cards should sit side by side on desktop and stack on mobile
NO_MATCH: show the two diffs side by side in the review ui

# prose for X in {columns, api responses, diffs, cards}; requiring an answer-noun did not
